newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria stocks off highs, slight correction seen.
newsitem.headline: Austria stocks off highs, slight correction seen.

text.p: Austrian shares ended moderately firmer on Monday after the ATX index failed to hold above the psychologically significant 1,100 points level, and traders said a slight correction towards 1,800 points was on the cards.

"The fact that we failed to break through 1,100 opens potential for a retracement down to around 1,080 points," said one. However, most market participants agreed that the underlying mood remained positive.

The ATX index of 21 blue chips rose 1.71 points to close at 1,094.71, down from an intraday high of 1,101.82. Among its constituents, eight decliners outnumbered seven gainers, six issues were unchanged.

Privatisation candidate Creditanstalt's preferred shares led the day's gainers amid hopes the six-year long battle to sell the country's number-two bank would come to an end soon. The stock was up 1.89 percent or 9.5 schillings at 511.
Brick-maker Wienerberger Baustoffindustrie was unchanged at 2,037.0 schillings following a report by Die Erste savings bank rating the group as a buy.

Oil and chemicals group OMV, the market's most heavily weighted stock, fell 3.5 schillings to 1,103.5, despite a forecast by chief executive Richard Schenz on Monday that the company would see another set of record earnings this year.
Fire-proof materials maker Radex led the day's decliners, falling 1.54 percent or five schillings to close at 319.5.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index rose 0.19 points to 419.35.
On the Vienna futures and options exchange, ATX contracts for November delivery were up 1.7 points at 1,097.9.
